entries.title: P0104 source and proof scope guard
entries.statement: Auffinger--Damron--Hanson Question 13 asks for chi<1/2 in d>=2 under suitable conditions on the iid lattice edge law F, and chi=1/3 in d=2. Their separate Question 15 asks for chi>0 in suitable dimensions; the canonical P0104 card combines them. The survey leaves both suitable conditions on F and the exact variance-scaling meaning of chi open. O(n/log n) variance gives a limiting logarithmic standard-deviation exponent of 1/2, so it is insufficient for strict subdiffusivity. A power saving in rotationally invariant Riemannian FPP and finite-size straight-path identities for lattice FPP do not establish a fixed-law lattice chi=1/3 result. Current October 2026 openness is not certified by this note.
assumptions: iid nonnegative nearest-neighbour lattice FPP for the original source questions
this is a source-scope and proof-obligation note, not a solution

source.excerpt: under suitable conditions on F, chi < 1/2. If d = 2, show that chi = 1/3

entries.title: Necessary variance-bound constant or onset tradeoff
entries.statement: For iid Uniform[1,1+epsilon] nearest-neighbour Z^d weights, d>=2, fixed epsilon in (0,1], put K=floor(2/epsilon). If C>0, integer N>=1 and theta<1 satisfy Var T(0,n e1)<=C Var(tau_e)n^theta for every integer n>=N, then either N>K or C>=K^(1-theta). This is necessary, not sufficient, for a fixed-law power bound.
entries.proof_text: If N<=K, the finite straight-path window applies at n=K because K epsilon<=2, giving Var T_K=K Var(tau_e). Insert this into the proposed inequality and cancel positive Var(tau_e), obtaining C>=K^(1-theta). The other possibility is N>K. For the straight-path identity, the direct route has at most n(1+epsilon) cost while every other route has at least n+2 edges of cost at least 1 by lattice parity.

relations.rationale: The source-scope note corrects the existing P0104 card's bundled Questions 13 and 15 and preserves its unverified open status.
The existing attempt explains the logarithmic-variance exponent gap without an FPP counterexample.
The finite-size lower bound on a variance prefactor or onset sharpens the law-uniformity caution but does not solve P0104.
The reviewed special case constrains any route that seeks law-uniform power variance bounds.
